common_name: Pinova Apple (Crisp Sweet-Tart German Modern Apple)

planting.note: Plant bare-root trees while dormant in late winter in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; best adapted to zones 5-8, providing a compatible pollinizer variety nearby.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible pollinizer variety nearby. Pinova was bred in Germany in the 1980s from crosses tracing back to Golden Delicious and Clivia, released for its crisp, dense, well-balanced sweet-tart flesh and attractive red-striped skin over a yellow background, quickly gaining popularity across Europe as a quality dessert apple with genuinely good storage life. The vigorous, productive tree bears reliably, and fruit holds its crisp texture and flavor well in cold storage for months, making it a satisfying choice for home orchardists wanting fresh apples well past the immediate harvest season. Harvest in mid to late fall once fruit fully colors, and store cool for the longest keeping quality.

Topaz was bred in the Czech Republic specifically for genetic resistance to apple scab, one of the most damaging and widespread apple diseases, giving it a real practical advantage for organic and low-spray home orchards in humid climates where scab pressure is heavy. The medium, yellow-green fruit blushed with orange-red has firm, crisp, notably tart-sweet flesh with good aromatic complexity, well regarded among disease-resistant modern apple varieties for genuinely good eating quality rather than resistance alone. The tree is productive and reliable; harvest in fall once fruit fully colors, and expect good storage life in proper cool conditions.

common_name: Rubinette Apple (Intensely Aromatic Swiss Dessert Apple)

planting.note: Plant bare-root trees while dormant in late winter in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; best adapted to zones 5-8, providing a compatible pollinizer variety nearby.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible pollinizer variety nearby. Rubinette is a Swiss apple with parentage tracing through both Golden Delicious and Cox's Orange Pippin, and it is widely regarded by connoisseurs as one of the most intensely aromatic and best-flavored modern apples available, delivering a complex, richly perfumed sweet-tart flavor reminiscent of its Cox heritage in a smaller, russet-blushed, red-striped fruit. The tree is only moderately productive compared with high-yield commercial varieties, a common tradeoff with exceptionally flavorful apples, but home orchardists focused on eating quality over sheer yield consider it well worth growing. Harvest in fall once fruit fully colors, and enjoy fresh, since the fruit's aromatic complexity is best appreciated soon after harvest.

Delbarestivale was bred by the Delbard nursery in France and released for ripening notably early in the season, giving gardeners fresh apples well ahead of the main fall harvest window most varieties occupy. The medium, bright red-striped fruit over a yellow-green background has crisp, juicy, sweet flesh with good, well-balanced flavor for such an early-season apple, since many early apples sacrifice flavor complexity for speed. The tree is productive and reliable; harvest in mid to late summer once fruit fully colors, and use fairly promptly, since early-season apples typically do not store as long as fall and winter varieties.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, providing a compatible pollinizer variety nearby. Elstar was bred in the Netherlands from a cross of Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie and has become one of the most widely planted apples across Europe, prized for crisp, juicy, aromatic flesh with a well-balanced sweet-tart flavor that has broad appeal for fresh eating, and it also performs well in baking, holding its shape reasonably well under heat. The medium, red-blushed fruit over a yellow-green background ripens in early to mid fall, and the productive, reliable tree has made it a commercial and home-orchard standard throughout its native growing region. Harvest once fruit fully colors, and store cool for good, though not exceptionally long, keeping quality.
